7. Carton and container: designing out medication errors
11. Converting an older-format label to PLR

questions.q: Which of these is NOT part of a product's labeling in US terms?
questions.why: Labeling is the written matter on or with the product. A study report supports the application but is not labeling.

questions.q: Who is the main reader of the prescribing information?
questions.why: The PI is written for prescribers and pharmacists; patient labeling is written for patients.

questions.q: Which regulation sets the PLR content and format requirements?
questions.why: 201.56 gives general requirements and 201.57 the specific PLR content and format.

questions.q: Who approves the exact wording of a prescription drug label in the US?
questions.why: Labeling is part of the approved application; FDA approves its wording.

questions.q: Medication Guides are governed by which part of 21 CFR?
questions.why: Part 208 covers Medication Guides for prescription drugs.

questions.q: The bar code requirement for drug labels is in:
questions.why: 201.25 requires a linear bar code containing the NDC.

questions.q: What does a "Training use only" watermark on this app's exports mean?
options: The label is a practice document and must not be used as a real label
The label is in draft at FDA
The label is for internal company use
questions.why: All products here are fictional and nothing is an approved label.

questions.q: Which reader is most likely to be under time pressure and confuse look-alike products?
options: A nurse choosing a vial from a shelf
A patient reading the leaflet at home
questions.why: Carton and container labels are designed for quick, accurate selection at the point of use.

questions.q: How long may Highlights be, not counting a boxed warning?
questions.why: Highlights must fit on one half page unless FDA grants a waiver.

questions.q: Which item comes right after the product title in Highlights?
questions.why: The year of initial US approval follows the product title.

questions.q: How does each Highlights statement point to the detail?
options: The FPI section number in parentheses
questions.why: Each statement ends with its FPI section number, for example (5.2).

questions.q: Section 3 of the FPI is:
questions.why: Sections 1 to 4 are Indications, Dosage and Administration, Dosage Forms and Strengths, Contraindications.

questions.q: If a product has no drug abuse concerns, what happens to section 9?
options: It is omitted and later sections keep their numbers
questions.why: Sections can be omitted when not applicable, but numbering never changes.

questions.q: The Highlights adverse reaction contact statement includes which FDA number?
questions.why: The statement names the manufacturer and FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088 or www.fda.gov/medwatch.

questions.q: Highlights end with:
options: The patient counselling statement and the revision date
questions.why: The counselling statement and "Revised: MM/YYYY" close Highlights.

questions.q: Which is the correct revision date format?
questions.why: Month and year: MM/YYYY.

questions.q: The Highlights summary of a boxed warning may be at most:
questions.why: The summary is limited to 20 lines.

questions.q: Which change can be listed in Recent Major Changes?
options: A new subsection in Warnings and Precautions
questions.why: Only the Boxed Warning and sections 1, 2, 4 and 5 can be listed.

questions.q: How long does a Recent Major Changes entry stay?
options: At least one year, removed at the first printing after that
questions.why: Entries stay at least a year after the change.

questions.q: A boxed warning heading must begin with:
questions.why: The heading begins "WARNING:" followed by the risk, in capitals.

questions.q: The Highlights boxed warning ends with:
options: "See full prescribing information for complete boxed warning."
questions.why: That closing line is required.

questions.q: Where does the full boxed warning sit in the FPI?
questions.why: It appears at the beginning of the FPI.

questions.q: A new risk is added as 5.6. Which of these does NOT normally need updating?
questions.why: Description covers the product's composition and is unaffected by a new risk.

questions.q: Each boxed warning risk in the FPI should refer to:
options: The relevant Warnings and Precautions subsection
questions.why: The box summarises; section 5 holds the detail.

questions.q: If a drug has no contraindications, section 4 says:
questions.why: Section 4 is never left out; it states "None." when there are none.

questions.q: Which is the correct PLR cross-reference style?
questions.why: Cross-references name the section and give its number in parentheses.

questions.q: 6.1 Clinical Trials Experience includes a standard statement that:
options: Rates from different trials cannot be compared directly
questions.why: The statement warns against comparing rates across trials.

questions.q: Where do spontaneous reports after approval usually go?
questions.why: Postmarketing reports are described in 6.2.

questions.q: A contraindication is appropriate when:
options: A side effect is common but mild
The risk clearly outweighs any possible benefit in that situation
The drug was not studied in a group
questions.why: Contraindications are for situations where the drug should not be used.

questions.q: You swap 5.2 and 5.3. What else must change?
options: Every cross-reference to 5.2 and 5.3, and the Highlights references
questions.why: References follow the numbers; the editor rewrites them when you reorder.

questions.q: Section 6 begins by listing:
options: Clinically significant reactions described elsewhere in the labeling
questions.why: It lists the serious reactions covered in other sections, with references.

questions.q: Which belongs in Warnings and Precautions?
options: How to monitor for and manage a serious risk
questions.why: Section 5 covers clinically significant risks and their management.

questions.q: When did the PLLR take effect?
questions.why: The Pregnancy and Lactation Labeling Rule took effect on 30 June 2015.

questions.q: Which of these may a PLR label still show?
questions.why: Letter categories were removed; 8.1 and 8.2 begin with a Risk Summary.

questions.q: 8.2 is titled:
questions.why: PLLR renamed the subsection Lactation.

questions.q: 8.3 covers:
options: Females and Males of Reproductive Potential
questions.why: 8.3 covers pregnancy testing, contraception and infertility.

questions.q: If a pregnancy exposure registry exists, where is it described?
questions.why: Registry information appears in 8.1 before the Risk Summary.

questions.q: The 8.1 Risk Summary states background rates of:
questions.why: Background risks for the population are given for context.

questions.q: Animal data supporting a pregnancy risk statement go under:
questions.why: Human and animal data are summarised under Data in 8.1 (with nonclinical detail in 13).

questions.q: An older-format label still shows "Pregnancy Category B". When converting to PLR you should:
options: Replace it with a Risk Summary and data
questions.why: PLR labels cannot use letter categories.

questions.q: A Medication Guide is required when:
options: FDA decides patient information is needed for safe and effective use, for one of the reasons in Part 208
questions.why: Part 208 sets out when FDA requires one.

questions.q: Which heading belongs in a Medication Guide?
options: "What is the most important information I should know about X?"
questions.why: Medication Guides use question headings in plain language.

questions.q: What must the carton say when a Medication Guide is required?
options: Instruct the dispenser to give the Medication Guide to each patient
questions.why: The label tells the dispenser to provide the Medication Guide.

questions.q: The Medication Guide side-effect statement mentions:
options: Reporting side effects to FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088
questions.why: It reads "Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects. You may report side effects to FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088."

questions.q: Which product type usually needs an IFU?
options: A prefilled pen or metered-dose inhaler
An oral solution in a bottle
questions.why: IFUs explain multi-step use of devices and complex products.

questions.q: Where in the PI is the prescriber told to advise reading the patient labeling?
questions.why: Section 17 opens with that advice.

questions.q: Status of FDA's Patient Medication Information (PMI) rule as of mid-2026:
questions.why: PMI was proposed in May 2023 and was still proposed in mid-2026.

questions.q: A Medication Guide states that it:
options: Has been approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration
questions.why: The approval statement is required.

questions.q: Which strength expression avoids a tenfold error?
questions.why: No trailing zeros, and a leading zero for values below 1.
questions.cite: FDA container and carton guidance (2022); ISMP list

questions.q: The established name on a carton must be at least:
options: The same size as the proprietary name
Half the size of the proprietary name
questions.why: 21 CFR 201.10(g)(2) sets the half-size minimum.

questions.q: For a 5 mL vial containing 50 mg, the strength reads:
questions.why: Injectables show the amount per total volume, then per mL.

questions.q: Which is a valid 10-digit NDC configuration?
questions.why: Valid configurations are 4-4-2, 5-3-2 and 5-4-1.

questions.q: The linear bar code on a prescription drug label must contain:
questions.why: 201.25 requires the NDC in a linear bar code.

questions.q: Which abbreviation is on the error-prone list?
questions.why: "U" can be misread as 0 or 4; write "units".

questions.q: "Rx only" on a label is required by:
questions.why: 201.100(b)(1) requires the "Rx only" symbol or statement.

questions.q: What is a proof check?
options: Comparing printed artwork word by word with the approved text
questions.why: Proofs are checked against approved text before release.

questions.q: SPL is based on which standard?
questions.why: Structured Product Labeling is an HL7 XML standard.

questions.q: How are PI sections identified in SPL?
questions.why: Each section carries a LOINC code.

questions.q: Can this app's XML export be submitted to FDA?
options: No, it is a practice file and not validated
questions.why: It is a teaching example, marked as such inside the file.

questions.q: Which public site shows SPL labels for marketed products?
questions.why: DailyMed publishes the SPL labeling FDA receives.

questions.q: Which difference from the reference label is permitted for a generic?
options: A shorter Warnings and Precautions section
A different list of inactive ingredients
questions.why: Inactive ingredients are among the permitted differences.

questions.q: A section viii statement lets a generic:
options: Omit an indication protected by a method-of-use patent
questions.why: The protected use is carved out of the label.

questions.q: After carving out indication 1.2, which must also go?
options: Dosing, study results and Highlights entries that depend on 1.2
questions.why: Every mention that depends on the carved indication goes.

questions.q: Who must update a generic label when the reference label changes?
questions.why: ANDA holders keep their labeling the same as the RLD.
questions.cite: FDA guidance on ANDA labeling updates (2024)

questions.q: Which section is usually different between a generic and its reference?
questions.why: How supplied details (NDCs, pack sizes) are the generic's own.

questions.q: The "Initial U.S. Approval" year on a generic label is:
options: The year the active moiety was first approved
questions.why: It refers to the active moiety, so it matches the reference.

questions.q: Under 505(o)(4), after FDA notifies the holder, the holder has how long to respond?
questions.why: The holder submits a supplement or a rebuttal within 30 days.

questions.q: If the holder disagrees with FDA's proposed change, what happens?
options: Discussions follow and FDA may order the change
questions.why: After discussions FDA can issue an order.

questions.q: What triggers a 505(o)(4) notification?
options: New safety information FDA believes should be in the labeling
questions.why: It is a safety labeling power.

questions.q: A holder wants to add a new warning quickly on its own initiative. Which route is typical?
questions.why: Strengthening safety wording can go through a CBE supplement.

questions.q: In conversion, "Nursing Mothers" content goes to:
questions.why: It becomes 8.2 Lactation, rewritten for PLLR.

questions.q: Old-format "Clinical Trials" results inside Clinical Pharmacology move to:
questions.why: Efficacy results belong in section 14.

questions.q: "Information for Patients" under Precautions moves to:
questions.why: Counselling content goes to section 17.

questions.q: Old-format drug interaction text under Precautions moves to:
questions.why: PLR gives drug interactions their own section.

questions.q: Which part is new when converting to PLR?
questions.why: The older format has no Highlights.

questions.q: Older-format labels are governed by:
questions.why: 201.80 covers the older format.

questions.q: Which code system names SPL section types such as Boxed Warning or Indications and Usage?
questions.why: Each SPL section carries a LOINC code for its type.

questions.q: What lets FDA and readers track the versions of one SPL document?
options: A set ID and a version number
questions.why: Every version of a label keeps the same set ID and gets the next version number.

questions.q: Where in an SPL file are the NDC, ingredients and packaging held?
questions.why: The product data elements describe the product in coded form, separate from the label text.

questions.q: How are SPL files sent to FDA?
options: Through the FDA Electronic Submissions Gateway
questions.why: SPL is submitted electronically through the ESG, inside the application or as a listing.

questions.q: Which regulation lists the permitted differences between a generic label and its reference?
questions.why: 314.94(a)(8)(iv) covers the labeling of an ANDA and the differences allowed.

questions.q: Under FDA's September 2023 revised draft guidance, what does a biosimilar's labeling carry?
options: One biosimilarity statement, whether or not the product is interchangeable
An interchangeability statement for interchangeable products
The reference product's brand name throughout
questions.why: The revised draft recommends the same biosimilarity statement for every biosimilar. It is a draft (Watch).
questions.cite: Labeling for Biosimilar and Interchangeable Biosimilar Products (revised draft, 2023)

questions.q: Where does FDA show which biosimilars are interchangeable?
questions.why: Interchangeability matters at pharmacy dispensing, so FDA points to the Purple Book.
questions.cite: FDA updated labeling recommendations for biosimilars

questions.q: Which law created FDA's authority under section 505(o)(4)?
questions.why: The Food and Drug Administration Amendments Act of 2007 added safety labeling change authority.
questions.cite: FD&C Act 505(o)(4); FDA guidance on safety labeling changes

questions.q: If discussions after a 505(o)(4) notice end without agreement, how soon may FDA order the change?
questions.why: After the discussion period FDA may issue an order within 15 days.

questions.q: What should the holder's response to a 505(o)(4) notice contain?
options: A labeling supplement with the change, or a statement of why it is not warranted
A Dear Health Care Provider letter only
questions.why: The holder either submits the change or rebuts within 30 days.

questions.q: What can follow a failure to comply with 505(o)(4)?
options: Civil money penalties, and the drug can be misbranded
questions.why: Violations can bring civil penalties, and the product can be deemed misbranded.

questions.q: In PLR, which section number is Contraindications?
questions.why: PLR sections: 1 Indications, 2 Dosage, 3 Forms and strengths, 4 Contraindications, 5 Warnings and precautions.

questions.q: When an older-format label is converted, which part must be written new?
questions.why: Highlights and the contents list have no older-format equivalent.
